correctness.rationale: For NB integer r>=3 and success p=t/(t+1), m=rt integer, the exact ratio beta_i=w_{m+i}/w_{m-i} satisfies beta_(i+1)/beta_i=(t/(t+1))^2 (m+i+r)(m-i+r-1)/((m+i+1)(m-i)); its cross difference is (2t+1)[i(i+1)-rt(t+1)] (independently expanded symbolically to zero). Thus the centered alpha_i differences w_{m+i}-w_{m-i} have one-turn U-shape. The universal integer-mean identity sum_{i=1}^m alpha_i=E[(X-2m)_+]>0 implies alpha1>0 when endpoint alpha_m<0. Endpoint is P(X>=2rt)>P(X=0): exact Vandermonde amplification covers t<=5 from quoted rational seeds (including direct tail bases), and for t>=6 a geometric-sum event gives comparison (t/(t+1))^(2rt)>(t+1)^-r from monotonic h(t). This supplies strict endpoints and one ordered positive-to-negative crossing for all stated integers, not only a finite sample.
